implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x00dd0bc1 and never reassigned; exactly ONE ordinary stack argument, at entry_ESP+0x4, occupying a four-byte slot that RET 0x4 pops. That argument is the deleting-destructor flag and only its low bit is examined: 0x00dd0bdc is `TEST BYTE PTR [ESP + 0x8],0x1` with ESP = entry-4, so the operand is entry+4 and the test is one byte wide against the immediate 0x01. Ghidra types the same slot `Stack[0x4]:1` and the machine-derived record reports one ordinary stack slot, observed true, sizes [1], stack_cleanup_bytes 4, cleanup owner callee -- all three agree with the listing. NOTE THE TENSION, which is real and is not smoothed over: the slot is four bytes wide (RET 0x4) but the machine reads one byte of it. Both are stated; see unresolved_questions item 2 for why the width is not observable from this body.
implementation.receiver_model: a 0x18-byte opaque run with NO member declared. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly displacements [0, 16, 20] with bounds_only true, max_offset 20, written_through 3, shape R-ALIAS -- three writes, three displacements, and not one read of the receiver anywhere in the 14 instructions, so nothing about the object's layout past 0x17 is reachable from this body. Naming a member for any of the three would be an identity claim the record cannot corroborate, so the model reaches each one by displacement. The three words are almost certainly the object's dispatch words; the argument for that is in mechanics.dispatch_word_argument and it is made from the image's own table contents, not from the record and not as a member name.
implementation.dispatch_model: none declared, and there is none to declare: abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and all 14 instructions are direct immediates or register moves. The body performs no virtual dispatch. What it does is STORE three dispatch words; see mechanics.dispatch_word_argument for why that is a layout argument and deliberately not a slot boundary.
implementation.dependency_note: both direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. 0x00642190 is already owned by reconstruction/metadata/pkg-sporepedia-safe-wave10/006422190.json and by the promoted src/reconstruction/pkg_sporepedia_safe_wave10/, which names it sporepedia_asset_destroy_00642190 with exactly this signature; this package reuses that name and signature so the two cannot drift, and asserts nothing about its interior. 0x00f47380 is already named free_00f47380 in the same promoted package as `void __cdecl (Word)`; the declaration here matches it exactly, also to prevent drift.

Sum 50, which is exactly the span from 0x00dd0bc0 to 0x00dd0bf1 inclusive and exactly ghidra_function.size_bytes. The two call rel32s decode to 0x00642190 (0x00dd0bdc - 0x78_94_4c) and 0x00f47380 (0x00dd0be9 + 0x17_67_97), the JZ rel8 is +9 landing on 0x00dd0bec, and the three immediates are 0x0147c9f8, 0x0147c9e8 and 0x0147cc78. function_extent.trailing_padding: the 0x0a bytes at 0x00dd0bf2..0x00dd0bfb are all 0xcc (INT3). So nothing falls through out of this body, the 50-byte extent is the whole function, and there is no second entry inside the padding.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI -- MOV ESI,ECX at 0x00dd0bc1, and every one of the five remaining receiver accesses (three stores, the argument pushed for 0x00f47380, and the returned word) goes through ESI. ECX is never used again. This is why the machine-derived receiver record reports register ECX with shape R-ALIAS: the base register it saw the receiver in is not the base register the listing's own memory operands name, and the listing's own displacement scan over ECX finds nothing.
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_1: entry_ESP+0x4 -- the deleting-destructor flag. Read as ONE BYTE at 0x00dd0bdc (`TEST BYTE PTR [ESP + 0x8],0x1`, ESP = entry-4) and masked with the immediate 0x01, so bit 0 of that byte is the only bit consulted. The slot itself is four bytes wide, fixed by 0x00dd0bef `RET 0x4`.
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_sites: two, both caller side: 0x00dd0be9 `ADD ESP,0x4` for the word pushed for 0x00f47380, and 0x00dd0bef `RET 0x4` for the flag word
observed_original_abi.return_semantics_machine: 0x00dd0bec `MOV EAX,ESI` executes on BOTH arms -- it sits after the join that 0x00dd0be1's JZ and the 0x00f47380 call both reach -- and ESI is the receiver alias from 0x00dd0bc1, never reassigned and not definable by either callee. So EAX holds the receiver on every path out of this body, and the C return type is a pointer to the receiver. The derived ABI record disagrees on the CLASSIFICATION, not on the listing: abi_derived.return is {register EAX, register_class aggregate_unknown, type null, void_possible false, confidence INFERRED} and the persisted projection renders that as return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX'. A register-to-register move of an aliased pointer is the easiest shape in the language for a width classifier to type, so this is recorded as a disagreement between the record's classifier and the listing, and the listing wins in the model. See validation.expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS and unresolved_questions item 1.

mechanics.body_shape: store three table pointers into the receiver at 0x00, 0x10 and 0x14; call the base destructor unconditionally; if bit 0 of the low byte of the flag word is set, hand the receiver to the deallocation port and drop the pushed word; return the receiver

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 14 instructions. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; 0x00dd0bc0's PUSH ESI makes it -4 and nothing else touches ESP until the 0x00f47380 call, so 0x00dd0bdc's [ESP+0x8] is -4+8 = entry+4, the first ordinary argument slot. RET 0x4 then consumes the return address plus that one four-byte word and the walk ends at +4, which balances.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements. (1) abi_derived.abi lists exactly one ordinary stack slot, at 'entry_ESP+0x4', with stack_cleanup_bytes 4 and side callee. (2) Ghidra types the same slot Stack[0x4]:1, one byte at that exact displacement. (3) The 24-byte body at 0x00642210 carries the byte-identical `PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX / ... / TEST BYTE PTR [esp+0x8],0x1 / ... / RET 0x4` shape with the same one-instruction prologue, so the same displacement resolves the same way there.

slots.entry-4: the saved ESI, pushed at 0x00dd0bc0 and popped at 0x00dd0bee
slots.entry+4: the flag word: four bytes wide (popped by RET 0x4), one byte read (TEST at 0x00dd0bdc), bit 0 of that byte the only bit examined

receiver_displacement.note: this is the body's COMPLETE memory surface. There is no read of the receiver anywhere in the 14 instructions, and no displacement outside these three. The three written words are each 0x04 bytes and 0x10 and 0x14 are adjacent, so 0x18 bytes is the exact reach -- which is why the modelled receiver is 0x18 bytes and not one byte more.
receiver_displacement.0x00: written at 0x00dd0bc3 with the immediate 0x0147c9f8 (6-byte encoding C7 06 F8 C9 47 01, so the displacement really is zero and is not a missing +4)
receiver_displacement.0x10: written at 0x00dd0bc9 with the immediate 0x0147c9e8 (7-byte encoding C7 46 10 ...)
receiver_displacement.0x14: written at 0x00dd0bd0 with the immediate 0x0147cc78 (7-byte encoding C7 46 14 ...)

dispatch_word_argument.claim: the three stored words are the receiver's dispatch words, at three subobject offsets, and this body is the destructor that installs them.
dispatch_word_argument.basis: the image's own words at the three addresses, read for this package, NOT any record in this repository:
readings: the word at 0x0147c9f8+0x00 is 0x00dd0bc0 -- this body's own address; +0x04 is 0x00641340, and the word at 0x0147ca70+0x50 is 0x00dd0bc0 with +0x04 again 0x00641340, so two separate tables in the image begin with the same (this body, 0x00641340) pair

the word at 0x0147c9e8+0x08 is 0x00dd0bb0, and 0x00dd0bb0 is the 8 bytes `83 e9 10 / e9 58 00 00 00` = SUB ECX,0x10; JMP 0x00dd0bc0 -- an adjust-and-jump thunk that subtracts exactly the 0x10 displacement of the word it sits in a table for
the word at 0x0147cc78+0x00 is 0x00dd0b40, and 0x00dd0b40 is `83 e9 14 / e9 78 00 00 00` = SUB ECX,0x14; JMP 0x00dd0bc0 -- the same thunk for the 0x14 displacement
dispatch_word_argument.conclusion: the word at receiver+0x00 comes from a table whose first entry is this body, and the words at +0x10 and +0x14 come from tables whose destructing entries are thunks that subtract exactly those two displacements and land here. That fixes the three displacements as three dispatch words at three subobject offsets -- one primary subobject at +0x00 and two further subobjects at +0x10 and +0x14 -- and it is why the model reaches them by displacement rather than by member name. It remains a LAYOUT argument: no record in this repository names the class, and the model asserts none.
dispatch_word_argument.what_is_NOT_claimed: that these are the right tables for any particular class, that any RTTI complete-object locator precedes them (the word immediately before 0x0147c9f8 is 0x00dd0590, a code address, so it is not a COL and none is claimed), or any class name at all.

mechanics.control_flow: exactly ONE conditional branch in the whole body: JZ 0x00dd0bec at 0x00dd0be1 (2 bytes, rel8 +9, target inside the recovered span 0x00dd0bc0..0x00dd0bf1). No unconditional jumps, no switch, no loop, no indirect transfer. The target 0x00dd0bec is the join, so the graph is a single diamond with the flag test as its condition and the deallocation as its taken arm.
mechanics.decompilation_agreement: unusual for this repository and worth recording: the live decompilation (`undefined4 * __thiscall FUN_00dd0bc0(undefined4 *param_1, byte param_2)`) agrees with the listing on every point this package models -- receiver in the first slot, one-byte second argument, the three table stores at +0x00/+0x10/+0x14, the unconditional base-destructor call, the bit-0 test, the conditional free of param_1, and `return param_1`. It disagrees only on naming (`FUN_00642190()` with no argument shown, where the listing shows the receiver left in ECX) and on the decompiler's own signature, which reports zero parameters. The listing was followed regardless, because that is the rule; the agreement raises confidence in nothing this package claims on its own and is noted only so a reviewer does not read it as corroboration the package needs.
mechanics.globals: three, and they are the three immediates. 0x0147c9f8, 0x0147c9e8 and 0x0147cc78 all fall in the data segment (0x01300000..0x02000000). The body READS none of them -- each is a MOV immediate, a store, not a load -- and the body reads no data-segment location of any kind. There is no other absolute operand in the 14 instructions.

direct_call_1.convention: __thiscall, receiver in ECX, no stack argument
direct_call_1.arguments: the receiver, still in ECX from 0x00dd0bc1. The instruction immediately before the call is a store (0x00dd0bd0), not a push, and the body never reloads ECX, so the callee receives the receiver as its hidden this and nothing is passed on the stack.
direct_call_1.cleanup: none on either side, fixed by the callee's own last two instructions `POP ESI / JMP 0x006412a0` (0x00642204, 0x00642205) -- a tail jump, which cannot be popping a caller's argument
direct_call_1.return: a word in EAX that this body never reads: the next instruction is a TEST against memory, and the only register the body reads afterwards is ESI, which the callee does not define
direct_call_1.callee_record: reconstruction/metadata/pkg-sporepedia-safe-wave10/006422190.json, promoted to src/reconstruction/pkg_sporepedia_safe_wave10/. Its own 0x5-byte-store prologue (PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX / three MOV-immediate stores at +0x00, +0x10, +0x14) is the same shape as this body's, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that the three displacements this body writes are a class's own dispatch words rather than three unrelated fields. Nothing about its interior is asserted here.

direct_call_2.reconstructed_name: sporepedia_free_00f47380 (the name used by the promoted pkg-sporepedia-safe-wave10, which types it `void __cdecl (Word)`)
direct_call_2.arguments: the receiver's own address, pushed by 0x00dd0be3 `PUSH ESI`. Not a pointer to a member and not a pointer to the receiver variable: the machine pushes the aliased receiver register itself, so the callee gets the object address. The model test asserts the address is exactly the receiver the caller supplied and is not receiver+0x10, receiver+0x14, or the address of the receiver variable.
direct_call_2.cleanup: caller-side, ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x00dd0be9, because the callee's terminator is a bare C3 (0x00f47394)
direct_call_2.return: nothing; the callee is `void` and the body does not read EAX afterwards
direct_call_2.callee_record: no metadata record for this address. Its 21-byte body was read from the image for this package: MOV EAX,[esp+4] / TEST EAX,EAX / JE / MOV ECX,[0x16c8b44] / PUSH EAX / CALL 0x009276c0 / RET. It null-checks its argument, and 0x006421d0 calls it the same way for the same purpose, so it is a deallocation port of this codebase's own. That null tolerance is a fact about the CALLEE and is asserted by nothing in this package.

mechanics.callee_order: stores (instructions 3, 4, 5) -> base destructor (6) -> flag test (7) -> deallocation (9, 10) -> join -> return. The base destruction is UNCONDITIONAL: it runs on both arms, and the flag governs only the deallocation. A reconstruction that made the base destructor conditional on the flag is killed by the test (16 assertion failures).
mechanics.write_ordering: all three stores precede BOTH calls. This is measured, not asserted: each of the two observers samples the three words and the rest of the object at the moment of its own call. A reconstruction that moved the stores to after the base destructor is killed by exactly that sampling (2 assertion failures) -- which is the smallest failure count of any mutation, and therefore the one measurement doing the most work in the whole test.
mechanics.not_modelled: the ten 0xcc bytes of INT3 padding after 0x00dd0bf1, which nothing can reach; the ten 0xcc bytes after 0x00642210 and 0x00dd0bb3/0x00dd0b48, which are the same padding around the neighbouring bodies; and 0x00dd0b50, the constructor, which installs the same three constants at the same three displacements and so corroborates the layout without being part of this target.

return_semantics.value: 0x00dd0bec `MOV EAX,ESI` on both arms, and ESI is the receiver alias from 0x00dd0bc1. The value is the object address, unconditionally.
return_semantics.ownership: The body's only ownership action is conditional: when bit 0 of the flag word is set it hands the receiver to the deallocation port. When it is clear the receiver is destroyed but NOT deallocated, which is the ordinary non-deleting destructor invocation. Nothing here acquires or releases any reference, and no record for this target speaks to the receiver's ownership rules.
return_semantics.lifetime: There is nothing frame-borne: no local object, no out parameter, no buffer. The three stores write into the caller's object, so the body's only output is the object's own state plus the possible deallocation.
return_semantics.why_a_pointer_and_not_void: because the instruction says so, on both arms, and both arms converge on it. It is not inferred from the shape of the function; the shape is what suggested looking.

evidence.decompiler_disagreements: only two, and neither touches a modelled point. (1) It shows FUN_00642190() with no argument; the listing shows the receiver left in ECX and nothing pushed, which is the same call. (2) Its own signature is `undefined FUN_00dd0bc0(void)` with parameter_count 0, while its decompilation body clearly takes two arguments. Everything else -- the three stores, their displacements, the bit-0 test, the conditional free, the returned pointer -- agrees with the listing. See mechanics.decompilation_agreement.
evidence.caller_note: There is no direct caller, and that is not a gap in the caller search: the xref export records four inbound references to 0x00dd0bc0 and all four are data or jump edges, not calls. Two are vtable slots -- 0x0147c9f8+0x00, where the table's own first word is this body, and 0x0147cac0 (= 0x0147ca30+0x90 = 0x0147ca70+0x50), whose table begins with the same (this body, 0x00641340) pair. The other two are the adjusting thunks 0x00dd0bb0 (`SUB ECX,0x10; JMP 0x00dd0bc0`, at 0x00dd0bb0..0x00dd0bb7) and 0x00dd0b40 (`SUB ECX,0x14; JMP 0x00dd0bc0`, at 0x00dd0b40..0x00dd0b47), which are what a virtual destructor call goes through. So the body is reached by dispatch and by two adjusting thunks, and by no direct call anywhere in the image.

unresolved_questions: The derived ABI record and the listing disagree on the RETURN CLASSIFICATION, and the listing wins. abi_derived.return is {register EAX, register_class aggregate_unknown, type null} and the persisted projection renders it as return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX'. The listing is unambiguous: 0x00dd0bec `MOV EAX,ESI` on both arms, with ESI the receiver alias, so the C type is a pointer to the receiver. A register-to-register move of an aliased pointer is the simplest shape there is for a width classifier, so this looks like a classifier limitation rather than a listing problem -- but it is recorded as a disagreement, not corrected, because no record in this repository adjudicates it and the validator reads the record. It costs the RETURN SEMANTICS check a PASS it would otherwise earn.

Is the flag a one-byte argument or a four-byte one? RET 0x4 pops four bytes, so the SLOT is four bytes wide; the TEST reads one byte of it, and both Ghidra's `Stack[0x4]:1` and the record's `sizes: [1]` call the argument one byte. This package declares the parameter `std::uint8_t` because that is what is read. It must be said plainly that the choice is NOT observable from this body: bit 0 of the low byte IS bit 0 of the four-byte slot, so no input whatsoever distinguishes a one-byte read from a four-byte read of bit 0, and a reconstruction declaring the parameter `int` would be behaviourally identical here. The four-byte slot is a fact; the one-byte reading of it is a fact; what a caller actually pushes is not established by this body.

Who calls this body, and with what flag? There is no direct caller anywhere in the image -- all four inbound xrefs are two vtable slots and two adjusting thunks -- so every invocation is a virtual call through a table, and the flag value each caller passes is not recoverable from this body. The ordinary C++ convention is a compiler-generated `delete` expression passing 1, but that is a convention, not a measurement, and no trace in this repository would settle it. This is also the reason the runtime gate below asks for a specific flag rather than just a specific receiver.

What class is this? The three stored constants, the two adjusting thunks that subtract 0x10 and 0x14, and the base destructor's identical three-store prologue together establish a class with one primary subobject at +0x00 and two further subobjects at +0x10 and +0x14 -- and nothing beyond that. No record in this repository names the class, no SDK symbol was recovered for 0x00dd0bc0 (ghidra_function.sdk_name is null), and the binary has no MSVC RTTI. The model therefore names no class and declares no member, and the `OpaqueSporepediaAsset` type name is a placeholder for 'the object this destructor runs on' and is NOT a claim that the SDK has a type of that name.

The record's vtables list (0x0147c9e8, 0x0147ca30, 0x0147ca70) does not include 0x0147c9f8, which IS the constant this body stores at receiver+0x00 and which the image shows beginning with this body's own address. Either the collector's table-start heuristic missed it or it classifies 0x0147c9f8 differently. This package did not resolve it: the constant was taken from the instruction's immediate and the table's contents from the image, and the record's list is reported unchanged. It is worth the integrator's attention because three of the four table addresses this body is associated with would then be mis-attributed.

Is 0x00641340, the word immediately after this body in both tables at 0x0147c9f8+0x04 and 0x0147ca70+0x54, the class's vector deleting destructor? Its 18 bytes read as `MOV EAX,[ECX] / MOV EDX,[ESP+4] / MOV EAX,[EAX+0xa0] / PUSH 0 / PUSH EDX / CALL EAX / RET 0x4`, i.e. it reads the receiver's own dispatch word, takes a slot at +0xa0 of it and calls it with the flag and a zero. That is the shape of a two-argument thiscall through a slot, which is what MSVC emits for a vector deleting destructor, and its adjacency to this body in two separate tables is what such a pair looks like. It is NOT claimed: 0x00641340 is a different VA, outside this target, and nothing in this package's scope was used to settle it.

Is the ten-byte 0xcc run at 0x00dd0bf2 the whole gap to the next function, or does the image carry a second entry inside it? The bytes are ten 0xcc and Ghidra's body_end is 0x00dd0bf1, so the two agree that there is no second entry -- but no disassembly of the padding was requested, and MSVC's padding is padding, so this is treated as settled.
Not fixable from this package, reported not chased: GLOBALS and EVIDENCE COVERAGE are structurally WARN. See validation.expected_reasons and known_blockers.

conditions: The original process is driven to an object of this class, once with the destructor flag 0 and once with it 1, so that both arms of 0x00dd0be1 execute in the live process.

A trace records the three words the object holds at +0x00, +0x10 and +0x14 immediately BEFORE 0x00dd0bd7 and immediately after it, to confirm the three stores replace the live table pointers with exactly 0x0147c9f8, 0x0147c9e8 and 0x0147cc78 and that nothing else on the object changes.
A trace records that 0x00642190 is entered with the receiver in ECX and with NO stack word pushed, which is the claim this package cannot check statically -- that the call site pushes nothing.
A trace records the address 0x00f47380 receives on each arm, and confirms it is the object address and not a member of it.

A trace confirms the returned EAX equals the receiver on BOTH arms, and in particular that it is returned on the non-deallocating arm too, which is the one place a deleting destructor is easy to get wrong.

A trace drives a real `delete` through the object's own dispatch word and confirms the object is both destroyed and deallocated, and separately confirms that a plain scope exit destroys it without deallocating -- the two live invocations this body exists to serve.

validation.compile_gate: clean build with zero warnings under -Wall -Wextra -Werror, test exit 0. g++ 16.2.1. The header compiles clean as its own translation unit under the same flags (through a one-line TU that includes it, because -Werror promotes the `#pragma once` of a main file to an error), and the .cpp compiles clean under clang++ -m32 with the same flags. NOT -Wpedantic-clean on GCC, and the cause is the prescribed calling-convention macro pattern rather than anything written here: GCC rejects `__attribute__((thiscall))` on a non-class free function under -Wattributes, which -Wpedantic promotes, so a two-line file containing only the prescribed #define block and a free function declaration fails. The mandated gate does not enable -Wpedantic and passes clean.
validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. Both direct callees are defined in the test as observers that record their arguments, count their calls, and sample the receiver's bytes at the moment of the call. Four behaviour cases: A the flag's bit 0 set; B the flag's bit 0 clear; C the two arms leave byte-identical objects, so the flag's only effect is the transfer; D six mixed calls settle and still change exactly three words. Ten refutation cases, M1..M10, listed in validation.mutation_checking. Constants V1..V13 check the model's own literals against the instruction operands they came from. A raw-call trampoline (inline asm, one four-byte push, ESP and EAX sampled around the call) drives the 18-row flag table, the return-value checks and the ABI measurement.

mutation_checking.method: the package was copied to /tmp/opencode/w08/mut/<name>, ONE deliberate defect was injected into one of the three files with a python string replacement, then rebuilt and rerun with the mandated command. 24 defects were injected in the first sweep, all killed. The three stores were then re-expressed (see validation.expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: the +0x00 literal removed and the three immediates inlined at the stores), so a SECOND sweep of 20 defects -- covering every defect class in the first sweep plus two new ones -- was run against the final .cpp. Every one of those 20 also died, with the same failure counts where the defect was the same. Zero survivors across both sweeps, 44 injections in total.

mutation_checking.survivors: none of the 24 injected defects survived.
mutations_that_could_not_be_expressed: changing the calling convention of either callee. The convention macros in the header are shared by the declaration and by the observer's definition, so declaring the port stdcall while the observer stays cdecl is a conflicting-declaration error, not a silent defect. That is a HARDER kill than a failing assertion, but it means the package cannot be built with the wrong port convention -- and it also means the model test does not, and cannot, exercise the caller-side `ADD ESP,0x4` of 0x00dd0be9. See unresolved_questions item 2's neighbour, recorded in the model test's own not-asserted list and in the header next to the declaration.

a signed-versus-unsigned read of the flag. `if (static_cast<int>(deleting_flag) < 0)` on a std::uint8_t parameter is rejected by the compiler itself under -Wtype-limits, which -Werror turns fatal, so the parameter cannot be re-read as signed without the build failing. The mask-table case (M3/M4) is what covers the substantive question, and it covers it with 18 rows.
mutation_checking.known_limits: The check that the flag is a one-byte read rather than a four-byte read is impossible by construction: bit 0 of the low byte IS bit 0 of the slot, so no input distinguishes them, and the test says so instead of pretending to check it. The order AMONG the three stores is not observable at any callee boundary and is not asserted; only that all three precede both calls, which is measured. The caller-side cleanup of the deallocation call is not observable through a black-box port for a leaf callee, and two mutations of the test's own port observer confirmed that rather than being asserted against it.

expected_reasons.ABI: PASS. abi_derived.verdict is ABI_INFERRED (not ABI_UNKNOWN) and conventions.confidence is INFERRED (not unknown/approximation), and both the persisted and the derived convention resolve to the key `thiscall`. The target span names PKG_SWARM_W1_00DD0BC0_THISCALL and the macro resolves through the header the .cpp includes by quoted name, so source_conventions contains thiscall and no claim is mismatched. The cdecl macro in the same header resolves to `cdecl`, which is also a claim the body makes and agrees with, so the two do not contradict each other.
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS. The source span names both machine targets and no others, because each callee adapter is declared with the address as an 8-hex-digit suffix on its own name (sporepedia_asset_destroy_00642190, sporepedia_free_00f47380), which is the convention validate._callee_addresses reads. That equals both machine oracles: the xref export's two out-edges, and the listing's two direct transfers. The span's own symbol re_00dd0bc0 also matches the callee-token pattern but is excluded by _callee_addresses as the target's own VA. edges_truncated and callees_truncated are both false. The three namespace-scope constants in the .cpp are kStore00Value, kStore10Value and kStore14Value -- no address suffix, deliberately, so they cannot be read as callees.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: WARN, and it is unavoidable from this body. The complete 14-instruction listing DOES name data-segment addresses -- the three immediates 0x0147c9f8, 0x0147c9e8 and 0x0147cc78 are all in 0x01300000..0x02000000 -- so the evidenced-absence arm cannot apply. The xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all (its only edge types are direct-call, thunk, computed-call and external), so there is no second machine side to corroborate them against and none is invented. The arm the source actually reaches is the one that reports agreement: three source data addresses appear in the machine listing, with read/write mode still needing per-access evidence. That is a more informative WARN than the alternative, and the source names exactly those three and nothing else in the data range.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: PASS. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly displacements [0, 16, 20] with bounds_only true, and the source span declares two of them, as `+ 0x10` and `+ 0x14` on the second and third stores. Nothing the source declares lies outside the record's bounds, and -- the part that took a decision -- the span NAMES no member, so the check reaches its grounded arm rather than the arm that warns about an uncorroborated field identity. That was a deliberate choice and it is not a dodge: the record is a set of displacements and says nothing about which member is which, and a store-only body cannot do better, so naming a member would be asserting an identity the evidence does not carry. The three constants are declared as named constants in the header and transcribed as literals at the three stores instead, and a value is not an identity. The span contains no `->member` or `.member` form and no `offsetof`. The +0x00 store declares NO displacement, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: the machine's own form for it is `C7 06`, a zero displacement with no operand in the listing, so a `+ 0x00` written in the source would be a hexadecimal literal the listing does not contain and would fail CONSTANTS. The offset is still tied -- the header's kReceiverWord00Displacement is 0x00 and the .cpp static_asserts it against the store's immediate. NOTE the corpus caveat the validator itself carries: the listing's memory operands name ESI, not the record's ECX, so a naive ECX-only displacement scan finds none; the record was produced with shape R-ALIAS precisely for this case and the alias-aware scan in evidence_fields is what reads it. Either way the declared displacements are inside the record's bounds, which is what the grounded arm needs, and declaring two of three still reaches that arm because what it requires is that `outside` be empty and that something be declared.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS. abi_derived.parse is {declared_count 14, unparsed 0, degraded false, flow_complete true}, so the listing counts as fully consumed and declared_count matches the listing's own length of 14. Every hexadecimal literal in the target span is compared by VALUE against the listing's, and the span presents exactly five: 0x10 and 0x14 (the two non-zero store displacements) and 0x0147c9f8, 0x0147c9e8 and 0x0147cc78 (the three MOV immediates, transcribed as literals at the stores so a reader can check them against the instruction, and static_asserted in the .cpp against the header's named constants). All five are in the 14-instruction listing, and source-minus-machine is empty -- checked directly against validate._hex_tokens before the source was finalised, which is how the missing +0x00 literal was caught and removed. The mask and the two cleanup sizes are named constants in the header (kDeletingFlagMask 0x01, kStackCleanupBytes 0x04, kPushedWordCleanupBytes 0x04), so no literal is emitted for them. The two adjusting-thunk addresses 0x00dd0bb0 and 0x00dd0b40 appear in the header, the model test and the comments -- all OUTSIDE the target span -- because neither appears in this body's listing and would otherwise fail this check. The word 'vtable' appears throughout the comments of the span; _hex_tokens strips comments, so that is inert, and it is used there because the comment is the accurate description.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. The one conditional branch in the complete listing, JZ 0x00dd0be1 -> 0x00dd0bec, targets an address inside the recovered body span 0x00dd0bc0..0x00dd0bf1, so the branch graph closes inside it. The source span declares `if`, and the keyword shape is explicitly not part of the verdict.
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS. The complete 14-instruction body names no indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand, and abi_derived.dispatch agrees at 0 indirect calls, 0 call offsets and 0 vtable-shaped loads. The source span was audited for the five slot-boundary tokens the check looks for -- load_slot, object_slot, shell_slot, vtable, slot[ -- and contains none in code. That took a naming decision: the three stored constants are named kObjectTableAt00 / kObjectTableAt10 / kObjectTableAt14, never anything containing 'vtable', so the token cannot appear in code even though the surrounding comments (stripped before the check) discuss dispatch words at length. No slot boundary is declared anywhere in this package.
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: WARN, and it is a disagreement between the record and the listing that this package cannot resolve in its own favour. The canonical claim is the first non-empty of return_type / return_semantics across the ABI sources; the persisted record's abi is an empty dict for this target, so the claim is the derived projection's return_semantics, 'unclassified_in_EAX'. The span's declared return type is `OpaqueSporepediaAsset*`. They are not the same string, so the check takes its semantically-renamed arm. The machine says otherwise and the model follows the machine: 0x00dd0bec `MOV EAX,ESI` on both arms, with ESI the receiver alias, is a pointer to the receiver. This was checked against the alternative route before the source was written -- evidence_returns.decide defers, by its own rule, whenever any ABI source carries a return_type or return_semantics claim, so that stricter path cannot adjudicate this target at all. Closing the warning would mean declaring a C type whose spelling equals the string 'unclassified_in_EAX', which is not a type. Reported, not chased. See unresolved_questions item 1.
